key_reveal_optionality.highlight: Lucid's market-based key-reveal deterrence deemed insufficient given MEV payoff variance; seeking protocol-level enforcement
Jannik: skeptical of enshrining a specific threshold scheme; cryptographic development still active, small validator committees are bribable/unobservably misbehaving
Consensus: Lucid's financial penalty for key withholding is probably not strong enough; stronger optionality protections needed

threshold_encryption_naive_scheme.highlight: Benedikt: for small N parties, naive scheme (secret-share symmetric key, encrypt one share per party) is viable; ciphertext size linear in N
CCA2 security mandatory for encrypted mempools (committee acts as decryption oracle); naive scheme can be made CCA2 via hybrid encryption + one-time signature
Reusing validator BLS keys for encryption is non-PQ and problematic; future hash-based validator keys cannot serve as threshold encryption keys
With PQ, nothing materially better than the naive scheme currently exists; non-PQ silent/batching schemes require a CRS ceremony

crs_ceremony_approach.highlight: Jan: CRS-based silent scheme preferred over DKG — avoids fixing party set, allows validators to join non-interactively by publishing per-key group elements
Gottfried: CRS ceremony complexity varies greatly; powers-of-tau is uniquely composable/low-interaction; not all CRS types share that property
Benedikt: CRS ceremony for a non-PQ solution is high effort for something likely replaced soon; naive scheme more realistic to ship

validator_whitelisted_key_publishers.highlight: Jannik: alternative to enshrined crypto — Lucid as-is but validators vote to whitelist trusted key-publisher entities
Gottfried: whitelist risks ossification — newcomers face chicken-and-egg problem gaining validator votes before proving reliability
Anders: validator voting on external entities creates cartelization pressure within the validator set; prior per-user trust model felt safer

action_items.action: Investigate how to achieve CCA2 security on the naive threshold scheme (hybrid encryption + one-time signature approach)
Further analyze validator-whitelisted key-publisher proposal: game theory, cartelization risk, builder behavior

decisions.decision: Two research directions confirmed: (1) naive PQ threshold encryption with CCA2, (2) Lucid + validator-whitelisted key publishers with cartelization analysis
